No validation here either - it just reconstructs the matrix from recovered cells.

Now let me verify my understanding by checking if data column sidecars are supposed to be complete or can be partial. Let me look at where data_column_sidecars come from in the first place:

Actually, wait! Line 4095-4098 checks if any of the FIRST half_columns (0..64) are missing. This is a different check - it ensures you have all columns in the range [0, 64), not just any 64 columns.

But this is only in ONE caller (HTTP API). Let me check the other caller (blob_reconstruction_pool) again:

The blob_reconstruction_pool path does NOT have the extra check (lines 4095-4098 in HTTP API). It only checks `available_columns.len() * 2 >= P::NumberOfColumns::USIZE` (line 42). Now let me verify whether the missing cells in a column is even possible. Looking at DataColumnSidecar structure again: ```rust pub column: ContiguousList, P::MaxBlobCommitmentsPerBlock>, ``` This is a variable-length list. So yes, a DataColumnSidecar can contain fewer cells than the maximum number of blobs. Let me check if there's any specification requirement that all columns must contain the same number of cells:

Let me understand the actual vulnerability better. In blob_reconstruction_pool/tasks.rs, the code doesn't validate that each individual blob has sufficient cells. Let me trace through what happens:

1. Code retrieves all available data column sidecars (line 30-35)
2. Checks if count >= 50% of total columns (line 42)
3. Converts columns to matrix entries (line 59-62)
4. Calls recover_matrix which groups by row_index (blob) and recovers each independently (line 64)

The issue is that **different blobs can have different numbers of available cells** depending on which columns are available, even if the total column count is ≥50%.
